title: runtime-load-synthesis-and-observable-signatures-2025
author: Marina Liu
content:
Overview

Purpose: A reproducible library of synthetic load shapes for the Redwood serving runtime, together with the telemetry signatures each one produces. It gives engineers and SREs a common vocabulary for diagnosing anomalies, designing alerts and tuning scheduler/kernel settings.

Audience: runtime engineers, performance SREs, the profiling team, and product teams running closed-loop experiments.

This page contains:
- Canonical load shapes with generator commands
- An observable signature matrix
- An experiment matrix and acceptance criteria for kernel/scheduler changes
- A quick triage playbook and ownership map

1) Canonical load shapes

Shapes are parameterized by concurrency (clients), typical sequence length, prompt entropy and inter-arrival distribution. Use loadkit with the flags below so runs are comparable.

A. Steady-state throughput (baseline)
- Constant QPS and uniform sequence length; calibrates per-token overhead and bandwidth.
- Parameters: qps=50, seq_len=128, concurrency=25 clients, token_gen_model=llamav2-13b
- loadkit run --shape steady --qps 50 --seq-len 128 --clients 25 --duration 15m --model llamav2-13b
- Runtime flags: --kv-cache=on --batching=continuous --batch-max-tokens=4096

B. Bursty microspikes
- 30s-2m bursts at 5-10x baseline QPS; exercises kernel preemption and queue admission.
- loadkit run --shape bursty --qps 50 --burst-mult 8 --burst-period 90s --seq-len 64 --duration 10m

C. Ramp-and-hold (scale events)
- Linear ramp from 1x to 10x QPS over 10 minutes, 5 minute hold, then decay; validates autoscaling.
- loadkit run --shape ramp --start-qps 5 --end-qps 500 --ramp-duration 10m --hold 5m --seq-len 256

D. Tail-heavy (sporadic large sequences)
- Short (32 token) and long (2048 token) requests, long ones at 2% frequency; finds sequence-length kernel breakpoints.
- loadkit run --shape tail-heavy --short 32 --long 2048 --long-rate 0.02 --qps 80 --duration 20m

E. Cold-fanout
- Many clients opening new sessions with no shared KV cache; exercises warmup paths and model load latency.
- loadkit run --shape cold-fanout --clients 500 --session-duration 10s --seq-len 64 --duration 15m

2) Observable signature matrix

Metrics (Prometheus / runtime telemetry):
- runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket
- runtime_request_duration_seconds_count
- runtime_kernel_queue_depth
- runtime_kernel_preemptions_total
- runtime_gpu_kernel_execute_time_seconds_sum
- runtime_kvcache_miss_rate
- runtime_batch_size_distribution
- runtime_dispatch_retries_total
- runtime_gpu_memory_fragmentation_ratio

Expected signatures
- Steady-state: stable p50/p95, batch size mode near the configured max, small steady queue depth, kvcache_miss_rate under 1%.
- Bursty spikes: p99 jumps, queue depth spikes, preemptions_total rises during bursts, batch sizes briefly drop to single digits.
- Ramp-and-hold: dispatch_retries_total grows linearly when admission thresholds are too low; backpressure at the ramp inflection if the autoscaler lags.
- Tail-heavy: p99/p999 dominated by long sequences; kernel_execute_time_seconds_sum climbs non-linearly and fragmentation may rise.
- Cold-fanout: higher model_load_latency, kvcache_miss_rate near 100% for new sessions, p50 elevated until caches warm.

PromQL examples:
- p99 latency: histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le))
- queue depth per node: max(runtime_kernel_queue_depth) by (node)
- kvcache miss rate: sum(rate(runtime_kvcache_miss_total[2m])) / sum(rate(runtime_kvcache_request_total[2m]))
- preemption spike detector (alert candidate): increase(runtime_kernel_preemptions_total[5m]) > 10

3) Experiment matrix and acceptance criteria

Run every cell when validating a scheduler or kernel change and record the deltas.

Columns: change-id, kernels toggled, scheduler flag, test-shape, measurement window, acceptance criteria

- CHG-3821 | per-request-kernel-hedging=on | priority-synthesis=v1 | bursty | 30m | p99 delta <= 10% at baseline; preemptions not increased by >20%
- CHG-3914 | simplified-quant-kernel | batch-max-tokens=4096 | tail-heavy | 1h | token throughput +/- 5%; fragmentation ratio decrease >= 5%

Recording: export a CSV with timestamp, node, metric, baseline_value, experimental_value, delta_pct, notes and store it in the runtime-experiments bucket as experiments/{change-id}/{date}.csv

4) Quick triage playbook

- Sudden p99 spike across nodes during a bursty test
  1. Check queue depth and preemptions. If queue depth > configured_batch_capacity for >60s, open the "kernel-contention-throttling-and-backpressure-playbook" runbook.
  2. Check whether runtime_batch_size_distribution collapsed; if so, escalate to the kernel team with the CHG-3821 results.
  3. For sustained queue depth plus memory pressure on a node: drain, gracefully restart the pod, then warmstart.

- Elevated kvcache_miss_rate
  1. Confirm the session affinity header in the request trace; if missing, follow the path back to the frontend.
  2. If affinity is present, inspect kvcache-shard-mapping indices and dry-run the shard rebalancer.

5) Ownership and contacts

- Runtime telemetry & dashboards: SRE Observability (owner: Connor Blake)
- Kernel scheduling experiments: Serving Runtime Kernel Team (owner: Marina Liu)
- Load generator & experiment infra: Perf Tools team (owner: Rashmi Verma)

6) Dashboards

- Load Shape Overview: qps, p50/p95/p99, batch_size_mode, kvcache_miss_rate per shape
- Node Health: queue depth heatmap, fragmentation ratio, dispatch_retries_total

7) Caveats

- Queue depth can briefly overshoot while admission control recalculates; only a >60s sustained increase is actionable.
- Long sequence tails skew histogram aggregates; look at per-sequence-length segments.
- Batch size collapse is usually a symptom, not the root cause; correlate with preemptions and dispatch retries.

8) Links

- Experiment CSV template: experiments/template-experiment-csv-v1.csv
- Loadkit repo: git@github.com:redwood/loadkit.git
- Telemetry queries: /dashboards/runtime-load-signatures

Appendix A - Experiment checklist
1) Create experiments/{change-id}/{date}/
2) Use an isolated staging cluster; tag telemetry with experiments/{change-id}
3) Run a 20 minute steady-state baseline and store the CSV
4) Run the target shapes and store CSVs
5) Compare metrics and complete the acceptance criteria form
6) Present at the weekly kernel-change sync and attach results to the PR

Appendix B - CLI snippets
- loadkit run --shape steady --qps 50 --seq-len 128 --clients 25 --duration 15m | tee baseline.csv
- promql-to-csv "histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(runtime_request_latency_seconds_bucket[1m])) by (le))" --from now-30m --to now --step 15s > p99.csv
